name: install
title: Install a non-electric bidet in about 15 minutes
sub: The six steps every attachment shares, and the one mistake that causes most leaks
footer: Sources: LUXE and Bio Bidet installation guides; fitment guides from Alpha and Bio Bidet; Good Housekeeping testers on install time. Always follow your model's manual.

items.head: Turn off and flush
items.body: Close the valve behind the toilet (clockwise) and flush to empty the tank. Keep a towel under the fill valve.

items.head: Check the fit first
items.body: Seat bolts about 5.5 in apart, at least 1.5 in of room behind them, and a tank that meets the bowl squarely.

items.head: Seat off, bidet on
items.body: Unbolt the seat, lay the attachment over the bolt holes, refit the seat. Firm, not cranked: plastic cracks.

items.head: Fit the T-adapter
items.body: T-adapter onto the fill valve, the supply hose onto the T, the bidet hose onto the branch. Washers seated flat.

items.head: Water on slowly
items.body: Open the valve a little at a time and watch every joint for a minute. A drip means re-seat, not overtighten.

items.head: First wash: lowest setting
items.body: Sit, then turn the knob slowly from the lowest pressure. Let the nozzle self-rinse before and after.

name: costs
title: What a bidet really costs over three years
sub: Purchase, water, electricity and parts, against the paper you no longer buy
footer: Paper spend $182 a year (OnePoll survey via StudyFinds, 2020), cut by half; water + sewer $15.44 per 1,000 gal (2026); power 18¢/kWh (EIA 2026); GFCI outlet about $210 (Angi). Our arithmetic; your numbers will differ.
